items.title: Japan Likely Sold Treasuries to Fund Record Yen Intervention
items.content: Japan likely sold a portion of its holdings of foreign securities, including US Treasuries, to finance its record currency intervention over the past month.
items.summary: Japan likely funded its record yen-buying intervention by selling foreign securities including US Treasuries, a move with significant global market implications.
items.detailed_summary_zh: 日本在过去一个月内很可能出售了包括美国国债在内的部分外国证券，以资助其创纪录的买入日元干预行动。
items.background_zh: 此前，美国与日本实施了十多年来首次协调干预，买入日元以阻止其跌至四十年低点。为筹集干预所需的美元资金，日本可能卖出了部分美国国债等外国证券。

items.title: China Injects Billions of Capital Into Banks, Insurers
items.content: China is injecting billions into its largest banks and insurers to shore up balance sheets and sustain growth in a slowing economy. Bloomberg's Sunny Bangia explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.summary: China is injecting billions into its largest banks and insurers to shore up balance sheets and support economic growth.
items.detailed_summary_zh: 彭博社报道，中国正在向国内最大银行和保险公司注入数十亿资本，以稳固其资产负债表并支撑放缓经济中的增长。
items.background_zh: 中国此次注资是在经济增长放缓背景下，由国家财政部门向主要银行和保险机构直接补充资本，以夯实其资产负债表并支持放贷能力。据《中国日报》报道，财政部将向中国进出口银行注资300亿元人民币；《卫报》报道则提到，三家国有银行已宣布合计获得2900亿元注资，金融业整体注资规模约为540亿美元。

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for September 7
items.content:
Oil climbed after the US attacked Iranian tankers and Tehran declared a new restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the waterway.

--- From rss ---
Asian stocks rose after US technology shares advanced on Friday. Oil climbed after the US and Iran traded tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
items.summary: Oil climbed after US attacked Iranian tankers and Tehran declared a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, threatening energy flows.
items.detailed_summary_zh: 美国袭击了伊朗油轮，伊朗随后宣布在霍尔木兹海峡外设立限制区，油价随之走高。市场担心这条全球重要石油运输通道的能源流动将受到持续干扰。
items.background_zh: 伊朗宣布在霍尔木兹海峡外设立新限制区，此前美国袭击了伊朗油轮，双方近期在这一关键石油运输水道互相攻击。

items.title: Canada Hits Back With New US Tariffs
items.content: Canada is set to impose new retaliatory tariffs of as much as 50% on US goods starting Sept. 8, targeting $27.6 billion of imports including steel, aluminum, pulp and paper, appliances and agricultural equipment. Bloomberg News Ottawa Bureau Chief Brian Platt tells Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason on Bloomberg This Weekend that the broader economic impact may be limited, but businesses tied to integrated supply chains, tourism and cross-border commerce could face sharper consequences as the cycle of retaliation continues. (Source: Bloomberg)
items.summary: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on $27.6 billion in US goods starting September 8, escalating trade tensions.

items.title: Prediction markets inch closer to the Supreme Court: State of Crypto
items.summary: Prediction markets are inching closer to a Supreme Court case, an incremental step in their legal and regulatory battle.
items.detailed_summary_zh: 据 CoinDesk 报道，预测市场正逐步接近由美国最高法院审理，这是其法律与监管斗争中的一个渐进进展。目前尚无最终裁决，相关影响仍待观望。
items.background_zh: 美国新泽西州总检察长已请求最高法院首次就预测市场（如 Kalshi、Polymarket）的监管权作出裁决；这类市场自 1990 年代以来在美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）批准下以“事件合约”形式合法运营。

items.title: Ukrainian police took down a crypto scam that stole up to $1 million a month
items.summary: Ukrainian police dismantled a crypto scam reportedly stealing up to $1 million monthly, highlighting ongoing crypto crime and enforcement.
items.detailed_summary_zh: 乌克兰警方捣毁了一个加密货币骗局，该骗局每月窃取的金额高达100万美元。
items.background_zh: 在乌克兰警方此次行动前，许多类似骗局采用“杀猪盘”模式：骗子通过约会或社交软件与受害者建立感情，再诱导其向虚假交易平台投钱。据涉案平台相关报道，运营者会手动制造交易记录并调整用户余额，让受害者以为投资在增长。

items.title: Better and Coinbase’s bitcoin-backed mortgages can reuse borrowers’ collateral
items.summary: Better and Coinbase are offering bitcoin-backed mortgages that allow borrowers to reuse their collateral.

items.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
items.content: Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments.
items.summary: Authors are contesting publishers' and agents' claims on payments from the Anthropic copyright settlement.
items.detailed_summary_zh: 据 TechCrunch 记者 Anthony Ha 于 2026 年 9 月 6 日报道，作者们正在对出版商和代理商提出的分享 Anthropic 版权和解金的主张表示反对。作者认为，出版商似乎试图从和解金中索取超出其公平份额的部分。这一争议发生在人工智能公司 Anthropic 与作者群体就版权侵权达成经济补偿和解的背景下。目前尚不清楚具体的分配比例或支付时间表。
items.background_zh: Anthropic 因未经许可使用受版权保护的书籍训练人工智能而面临集体诉讼，最终达成约 15 亿美元的和解，并于 2026 年 7 月获美国加州北区联邦地区法院批准。该和解覆盖超过 48.2 万本书，和解管理人正在厘清各书权利归属；但许多作者发现，出版社和文学经纪人已对同一笔款项提交了竞争性申索，部分原因是出版行业的权利记录不完整。这解释了作者为何抗议出版社与经纪人试图从和解金中分走更大份额。

items.title: Travis Kalanick’s Atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business
items.content: The Uber founder has said that Atoms will allow him to complete "unfinished business."
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Travis Kalanick's startup Atoms might enter the robotaxi business, but provides little beyond speculation.
items.detailed_summary_zh: TechCrunch报道称，Uber联合创始人Travis Kalanick的初创公司Atoms可能进入自动驾驶出租车（robotaxi）行业，但报道基本停留在猜测层面，缺乏具体证据。Kalanick仅表示Atoms将帮助他完成“未竟事业”，并未透露商业化时间表、技术路线或合作方。目前没有任何确认的运营计划或财务细节，因此该消息尚不足以构成确定性的行业动向。若属实，这将是Kalanick在出行领域的最新押注，但目前的公开信息相当有限。
items.background_zh: Travis Kalanick是Uber的联合创始人，曾主导Uber早期的自动驾驶汽车项目，但在2017年因争议离职。他的新创公司Atoms今年夏天宣布获得由Andreessen Horowitz领投的17亿美元融资，而Kalanick曾表示Atoms将帮助他完成“未完成的事业”。据英国《金融时报》报道，Atoms正考虑开发Robotaxi技术，并可能与Uber自动驾驶团队的前成员合作，这标志着Kalanick可能重返出行市场。

items.title: Your intellectual fly is open (2025)
items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[jeremyjh]: These are all important points and I love the analogy. But there is an even bigger issue with having LLMs write for you: Writing is thinking. Thinking and deciding. There have been many times when I start out writing something substantial - could be an email, a blog post, a software design document, anything - when my own views substantially changed during the writing process. Writing forces you to serialize your thoughts - and you can't always trust the gestalt. Reviewing gives you the ...

[dynm]: I'm a bit skeptical of arguments of the form, "You should not use LLMs without disclosure because LLMs at bad at writing." My reasoning is: If LLMs get better at writing—which I think is extremely likely—will you switch positions and say that now using LLMs without disclosure is A-OK? Surely  some  people are willing to bite that bullet and say yes. But for most people, my guess is that the answer will remain no. Thus, I tend to think that the "real" reason most of us...

[jgrahamc]: I think the most important line in this post is:  But LLMs are also lousy writers and (most importantly!) they are not you.  When I was editing the Cloudflare blog I imposed very little in terms of style so that the style of each individual writer could come through. It was almost as important as the actual content that the reader could feel that an actual individual wrote the text (with all their personal quirks intact).

[ericbarrett]: If I may compare written work to restaurants, a title and byline are like the storefront; I get an idea of what's being served, and if I'm hungry, I'll walk in and order. Sometimes the meal is amazing. Usually it's pretty good. Occasionally it's bland, or even bad, but not often enough to discourage future ventures; of course, I'm unlikely to revisit that particular proprietor. With LLM writing there's an additional outcome. I walk in and the walls are pleas...

[wj]: I don’t want to read content written by AI. A feature I would like on LinkedIn would be a 100% verified human content flag for users. LinkedIn can then do the scans and flip that to false for any users it catches posting AI assisted content. Let me filter that out of the feed. If we don’t do something to maintain some standard of discourse, we lose intellectually and as a piece of our humanity. LinkedIn is the only social media I use and it is on thin ice.
items.background_zh: 这篇博客借着“裤子拉链没拉”的比喻，讨论越来越多人在写博客、邮件或设计文档时使用LLM却不加说明。作者认为，问题不只是要不要披露，而是这样的文字已经不再真正属于作者本人。
